title: Dual-System Read-Your-Own-Writes Violation
pattern: Writing to the primary system of record and subsequently reading the same key from an asynchronously replicated migration target system.
why_bad: Due to replication lag, the read from the target database will return stale or missing data, violating read-after-write (read-your-writes) consistency and breaking application invariants [191, 659].
detection: A write method call on client A followed within the same call graph or session by a read method call on client B for the same entity key, when B is an asynchronous replica or target of A.
counterexample: Valid if the application explicitly tolerates stale reads and does not use the retrieved value for critical decision-making. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
source: Designing Data-Intensive Applications, Chapter 5, "Eventual consistency - Read-after-write consistency" [191, 659]
